source_title: Being told I’ve made no positive changes or progress since mom died four months ago
query: My mother died four months ago and I have no remaining family. Her friends are trying to support me, but they have fixed ideas about what recovery should look like. The bereavement triggered a severe chronic-illness flare, so I cannot currently work or leave the house to socialize. They think going back to work and socializing would improve both my health and grief, and one told me I have made no positive changes. How do I tell whether I am stuck or simply ill and grieving?
why_unprimed: The query leaves open whether avoidance, physical incapacity, depression, grief, social pressure, or a mixture is responsible and does not tell the bot to validate or challenge the friends.
first_route: Assess medical status, physical cost, safety, and basic functioning separately from grief.
Treat return to work and visible socializing as hypotheses, not outcome definitions.
Identify accessible forms of connection and support.
Assess whether friends are imposing performance demands or offering feasible help.
Use inner work only adjunctively and do not prescribe pushing through an underassessed illness.
defect_found: No new topology defect after maps 00, 12, and 13. This case validates the chronic-illness/grief boundary.
implemented_improvement: No new branch; retained as a regression test against psychologizing physical limitation or using productivity as grief recovery.
regression_assertions: The bot does not call the illness avoidance or a guard from the post.
The bot does not define progress as returning to work or leaving home.
The bot checks medical and functional information.
The bot supports connection in physically accessible forms.
The bot does not force a universal grief timetable.
